Solving trigonometric equations

Trigonometric functions repeat, so an equation such as sin⁡x=12 has infinitely many solutions. This solver handles equations of the form a f(bx+c)+d=k, where f is sine, cosine or tangent. It isolates the function, finds the principal value (exactly, when it is a standard angle), writes the general solution and lists every solution in one full turn, [0,2π) or [0∘,360∘).

Try changing the input

Change b from 1 to 2 or 3 in cos⁡(bx)=32: the graph oscillates faster and the number of solutions in one turn doubles or triples.

Method and general solutions

  1. Isolate the function: f(u)=r=k−da, where u=bx+c.
  2. For sine and cosine a solution exists only if −1≤r≤1.
  3. Write all solutions for u (with n any integer):
sin⁡u=r: u=sin⁡−1r+2πn or u=π−sin⁡−1r+2πn
cos⁡u=r: u=±cos⁡−1r+2πntan⁡u=r: u=tan⁡−1r+πn
  1. Solve u=bx+c for x and keep the values in the required interval.

Worked example

Solve 2sin⁡x−1=0 on [0,2π)

Step 1 — Isolate

sin⁡x=12

Step 2 — Principal value and its partner

x=π6orx=π−π6=5π6

Step 3 — General solution

x=π6+2πn,x=5π6+2πn

Assumptions, domain and rounding

  • Supported form only: a f(bx+c)+d=k with f∈{sin⁡,cos⁡,tan⁡}, a≠0, b≠0.
  • Constants may be written as expressions such as sqrt(3)/2 or pi/4; the phase c is in radians.
  • Each listed solution is checked by substitution. Standard angles are shown exactly as multiples of π; others are rounded to 6 decimal places.
